rv.q: This production succeeds in dangling all of those tempting carrots while keeping it mournfully funny.
It is a respectful rather than a revelatory evening, but this is, nevertheless, a welcome homecoming.
While there is nothing wildly wrong with this touring revival from the director Peter Reid for the Irish company AC Productions, it is accomplished rather than distinguished.
AC Productions’ bizarrely thought-provoking revival paid perfect homage to the show that caused such uproar in the very same theatre over half a century before.

It’s a solid staging of a work that feels eternally insightful into the absurdity of the human condition, and yet at the same time one which doesn’t offer any especially sharp or fresh insights into the play.

cn.t: Beckett's classic returns to its original London home in a competent but overly familiar production that lacks the shock value of its 1955 debut. Critics find the play timeless, but this staging feels safe and predictable.
